pillars.title: Engineering AI solutions around real business problems.
pillars.intro: Four kinds of problem I build for. Each names the work on this site that shows it.

items.title: AI workflow automation
items.problem: People spend hours sorting, summarising and answering routine items by hand: emails, requests, reports.
items.solution: An LLM pipeline that labels, summarises and drafts, with clear rules for what a person must still decide.
items.value: Less time on routine work, with urgent items still reviewed by a person.

items.title: Knowledge and retrieval systems
items.problem: Answers live across documents, past messages and the web, and a model on its own answers from stale memory.
items.solution: Retrieval and search tools that put the right context in front of the model, with sources cited.
items.value: Answers people can check, built on current information.

items.title: AI agents and intelligent applications
items.problem: Multi-step tasks (research, comparison, monitoring) need several tools and judgement, not one prompt.
items.solution: An agent loop with typed tools, caching, provider fallbacks and progress the user can follow.
items.value: Research and lookups that run in minutes and show their working.

items.title: Data integration and messy-data cleanup
items.problem: Business data sits in spreadsheets with mixed formats, missing values and inconsistent labels.
items.solution: Pipelines that parse, profile and flag bad records instead of silently changing them, then compute KPIs in code.
items.value: Numbers people can trust, and a clear list of what's wrong with the data.

cases.title: Real systems, the decisions behind them, and what still isn't solved.
cases.intro: Each case study covers the problem, the architecture, the hard parts, how it handles failure, and an honest account of what's measured and what isn't.

process.title: From a bottleneck to a system people rely on.

steps.title: Discover
steps.text: Understand the workflow, the systems, the data and where time is really lost, before choosing any tool.
steps.example: TabulaView.ai started from what breaks in real spreadsheets: ten kinds of 'missing', Indian digit grouping, day-first dates.

steps.title: Architect
steps.text: Pick the simplest design that fits the constraints: cost, rate limits, data privacy, who maintains it.
steps.example: TabulaView.ai keeps no files on the server: the browser re-sends the file, so 'we don't store your data' is literally true.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.text: Connect the APIs, databases and AI services the work depends on, each behind a clear interface.
steps.example: Lumen wires 8 external tools behind one cached interface the agent can call.

steps.title: Deploy
steps.text: Ship it with tests, timeouts and fallbacks, so one failing provider doesn't take the system down.
steps.example: TabulaView.ai is live on Vercel with 309 backend tests and a Groq → NVIDIA → rules fallback.

steps.title: Optimize
steps.text: Measure it, compare against a baseline and fix what the numbers show, including when the AI loses.
steps.example: TabulaView.ai's scorecard showed the AI analyst scoring 69.6 and 75.6 against the rules' 100, so the rules built the dashboard.

supporting.title: Applied machine learning and smaller builds

items.name: AI Email Assistant
items.text: Gmail + Gemini + ChromaDB: summarises, labels and drafts replies, and leaves urgent mail to a person.
items.fact: 4 LLM tasks per email · structured JSON labels

items.name: H1N1 and seasonal flu vaccine prediction
items.text: Predicts vaccine uptake from survey answers, with imputation and encoding fitted inside cross-validation to avoid leakage.
items.fact: Test ROC-AUC 0.835 (H1N1) and 0.861 (seasonal), from the notebook's saved outputs
items.note: Repo kept private until the notebook is cleaned up

items.name: Walking vs running classification
items.text: Classifies activity from wrist accelerometer and gyroscope readings, comparing logistic regression, random forest, an MLP and an LSTM.
items.fact: 88,588 sensor readings · random forest 98.8% test accuracy on 17,718 held-out rows (saved notebook output)

profile.title: Engineering at the intersection of AI, systems and business.
profile.summary: AI engineer with 13 months of internships in agentic AI and data science, and a B.Pharm from BIT Mesra. I build LLM features into tested, deployed applications, and I'm aiming that work at healthcare and operations data.

points: Built Lumen, a research agent using a Deep Agents (LangGraph) ReAct loop across 8 custom tools with a 3-tier search fallback (Exa, Tavily, DuckDuckGo).
Built 14 endpoints across 2 FastAPI services, streaming agent progress to a React/TypeScript UI over Server-Sent Events with 4 response block types.
Implemented Redis caching with per-tool expiry from 5 minutes to 24 hours, and modelled 3 core entities in PostgreSQL with JWT authentication.
Delivered 4 end-to-end machine learning projects across healthcare, motion-sensor, gaming and image data, from EDA to model evaluation.
Processed datasets of up to 88,588 records with Python and SQL: joins, aggregations, imputation and consistency checks.
Presented trends and model results through KPI reports and dashboards in Power BI and Tableau.
